Our Independent School & How to Apply/Re-Enroll

### our Independent School - How to apply/re-enroll

**First, why should you homeschool under the CHESS Independent School?**

- **Accountability to a private school institution instead of to a public-school/government institution.**

- **Attendance records/other required records maintained by our Independent School instead of by the state.**

- **Enrollment in the CHESS Independent School fulfills the State of Colorado compulsory school attendance law. (Compulsory school age for Colorado is age 6 by August 1st. Please see** [HSLDA](https://hslda.org/post/compulsory-school-age-in-colorado).)

- **15% HSLDA membership Discount:** HSLDA is a non-profit advocacy organization that makes homeschooling possible by protecting homeschooling families and equipping them to provide the best educational experience for their children. They have been trusted for over 35 years to care for homeschooling families, safeguarding their freedom and securing the future of home education. Families who are enrolled in our Independent School will be given a code to present to HSLDA to receive a 15% HSLDA membership discount.


### **ALSO IMPORTANT**

- Re-enrollment with the Colorado Heritage Independent School is done on a yearly basis.

- Our Philosophy, Statement of faith, and Acceptance Policy

  - Our Philosophy

    _At Colorado Heritage, we believe that God has given parents the responsibility to lead the academic and spiritual education of their children. With this in mind, we have designed our Independent School, Academy, and other services, with maximum academic flexibility while giving you the support, and accountability_ **_you_** _chose._

  - Please see our [Statement of Faith and Acceptance Policy](https://www.coloradoheritage.org/our-beliefs-1).

### Important Information About Our Academy and how to apply

_Colorado Heritage Education School System is a private Christian School serving homeschooling families._

- All subjects will be taught based on the truths of the Holy Scriptures.  (2 Timothy 3:16-17)

- Faculty, staff, and board members will provide a clear model of the biblical Christian life. (Matthew 22:37-40)

- Faculty, staff, and board members will encourage students and families to grow in their Christian walk and to seek God through Jesus Christ, the Savior. (Matthew 28:18-20, Matthew 19:13-15)


The God of the Bible is Truth and is the source of all Truth, whether spiritual, moral, philosophical, or scientific. Therefore, at Colorado Heritage, we require that our pedagogy is grounded in God’s Truth as expressed in the Scriptures. The curriculum and books we choose for our classes, the syllabi we create, our classroom instruction, assignments, homework, projects, performances, etc. will reverently reflect His truth, point to His glory, and express thankfulness for - and stress our need for - the Savior, Jesus Christ.

### VISION STATEMENT

Colorado Heritage desires that our students grow in their knowledge of our Creator and Savior through classroom instruction and interaction and that they will live out that knowledge in every aspect of their lives.

### MISSION

Colorado Heritage seeks to support homeschooling families as their students pursue the knowledge of God - the Creator and  Savior - through academics.

### MOTTO

Pursuing the Knowledge of God

* * *

### Colorado Heritage is a private Christian School

- Our Academy provides a variety of quality classes in order to meet the academic needs of homeschooling families. We hold to traditional Judeo-Christian values as seen in our [Our Beliefs](https://www.coloradoheritage.org/our-beliefs-1) and [Acceptance Policy](https://www.coloradoheritage.org/acceptance-and-eligibility-policy-1).

- In our 30+ year history, Colorado Heritage has been providing quality enrichment and core classes to K - 12 students.

- We offer science, math, history, Bible classes, literature, computer, art, music, drama, PE classes, and more.


### Why Colorado Heritage Academy?

**Our Teachers**

Our teachers are godly individuals and instruct from a Christian worldview with the belief that God is honored through spiritual growth and academic excellence

**Our Staff**

Our knowledgeable Christian staff will encourage and support you in your educational pursuits

**Our Board**

Our team of Christian board members faithfully labor in all aspects of guiding, supporting, and maintaining the spiritual, educational, and administrative health of our school.

**Our Fellowship**

Our hallways, lunch rooms, fellowship rooms, and recess times are always times of invaluable fellowship for both students and parents. Our special school events bless participants and observers alike. Smiling faces and encouraging words are one of the hallmarks of Colorado Heritage.

* * *

### **Our Philosophy,**

### **statement of faith, and Acceptance Policy**

**Our Philosophy**

At Colorado Heritage, we believe that God has given parents the responsibility to lead the academic and spiritual education of their children. With this in mind, we have designed our Academy, Diploma Program, Independent School, and other services to give maximum academic flexibility with the support and accountability **you** choose and that also ensure state education law compliance for those who are enrolled in our Independent School.

**Statement of Faith and Acceptance and Eligibility for Continued Enrollment Policy**

Please see our [Statement of Faith and Acceptance Policy](https://www.coloradoheritage.org/our-beliefs-1) under ABOUT US/Our Beliefs in the main menu.

* * *

### Are you a _new family_ (Prospective family\*) interested in our Academy? Please read below and follow the instructions.

**\*You are considered a prospective family: If your family is 1) not currently enrolled in our Academy or 2) has not attended our Academy in the past year, or 3) is not a current member of our Independent School and you would like to enroll your student(s) in our school.**

![](/api/media/files/b86f8ba9c84160df0af8cb978e188b1533a8ae1001d579bcab06381fcc49fd82.webp)

### High School Diploma Program

**Since 1991**, Colorado Heritage has been helping students succeed in their high school years and has graduated over 500 students. Seventy-five percent of our graduates have continued their education at a college or university, or academy. Colorado Heritage has earned a solid reputation among the academic community.

_We are thankful to be a part of our students’ academic success, but our greatest joy is seeing our students grow in godly character and in their relationship with the Lord Jesus Christ._

**How We Can Help**

The high school years play an important role in a student's future. Homeschooling in these years can become a substantial challenge. Our Diploma Program gives parents confidence to continue educating their children through the high school years.

For parents who are seeking to optimize their high school student's academic success while continuing to build upon a spiritual foundation, the Colorado Heritage Diploma Program may be a good fit.

**Private High School Transcript & Graduation Ceremony**

Our Diploma Program provides home-educated high school students with a 4-year high school plan that challenges and encourages both academically and spiritually. Many of our Diploma Program students pursue much of their course work through our [Academy](https://www.coloradoheritage.org/academy) along with classes taken at home.

Upon successfully completing our Diploma Program, students will receive a _private Christian school transcript_ and have the option of participating in our graduation ceremony. Colleges and other institutions highly esteem our high school graduates.

**Diploma Level Options**

Our Diploma Program offers four diploma tracks: **Diploma, Honors, High Honors, and Highest Honors**. Each program provides a framework to assist students in successfully completing high school graduation requirements while considering their gifts, interests, and future goals.

- The **General Diploma Option** meets minimum admissions requirements for most post-secondary institutions and provides greater flexibility in elective coursework.

- The **Honors Diploma Options** follow rigorous schedules of Colorado Heritage requirements in addition to our basic academic coursework.


**Four-Year Plan:** The Diploma Program offers a diverse and customizable four-year plan.

**Transfer Students:** Students who wish to transfer into our Diploma Program must provide us with a transcript from their previous high school year(s) and/or home records. We will evaluate the transcript to determine if our Diploma Program is a good fit. _Please provide the transcript to us before you schedule a Diploma Program meeting with us._

If you are a **new** family seeking enrollment in our Diploma Program, please use the below button to apply or set up a meeting to learn more. Transcripts are not necessary for an informational meeting but could be helpful. The Apply Now button will take you to our New Applicant Portal, which can also be found in our main menu.

If you are a **current** family seeking enrollment in our Diploma Program, please use the Schedule a Meeting button below.

### **Please note**

Please read our [Statement of Faith and Acceptance Policy](https://www.coloradoheritage.org/our-beliefs-1) in our main menu under ABOUT US/Our Beliefs.

[Apply Now](https://app.praxischool.com/site_login.php?s=1300)

### Tuition, Fees, and Scholarship Information

![](/api/media/files/cad4af3e05605553fe59bc81b15bf41f42a8d5592d6534cf6955e99c268d0aa5.webp)

* * *

**SCHOLARSHIPS and CHRISTIAN EDUCATION**

**Scholarships for our classes are available to qualifying families who have been accepted into our school. Economic times the past several years have been very hard on all of us. However, Christian education is vital for our children.**

**We encourage our families to assess their spending priorities and then apply for a scholarship if financial needs are a challenge.**

**_“Free Education”?_** **_Our goal is to support and encourage CHRISTIAN education._ Public (government) schools offer “free” K-12 education. The money to run these “free” schools comes out of _your_ pocket. However, you don’t have much to say about what is being taught to your children in these “free” schools, because once the government gets your money, they think it is _their_ money. They also tend to think (at the core) that _your_ children are _their_ children.**

**“Free” education from government-run schools comes with strings attached - they make the rules. And quite often, frankly, it is our precious students who end up paying a heavy price for this “free” education, as they are often subjected to ungodly indoctrination.**

**Christian family, CHESS is here to support you in giving your homeschooling student a solid, exemplary Christian education. Our teachers are stellar. Our school requires the very best from our students, and we require of ourselves the very best in serving our students and families. Please consider CHESS as you plan your homeschooling year.**

**Each year, we hold fundraisers for our scholarship fund. We highly encourage those who receive scholarships from us to participate in these fundraisers. Thank you.**

pages.markdown:
### Colorado Heritage Dress Code

**Why a Dress Code?** **The goal of our dress code is to glorify God and to be a blessing to our students.**

**Academic Success** **It is our observation that in certain life-callings, we are required to “dress for the job” and that being dressed for the job creates an atmosphere of responsibility, professionalism, and dedication.  Colorado Heritage believes this atmosphere of excellence is greatly beneficial for our students’ goals of achieving academic success.  Our research into attire for academic settings has led us to firmly believe that when students dress in clothing that is not their everyday clothing (play cloths, jeans, etc.), but rather in that which is geared towards a professional mindset, the education atmosphere is more conducive for mental alertness and creates a higher dedication and desire to learn.**

**Modesty** **Along with creating a successful learning atmosphere, we also desire to maintain an atmosphere of modesty. We understand that modesty has been given many definitions and is approached in many different ways and through many different philosophies. We do not believe that dressing a certain way saves a person’s soul nor can earn “points” with God. Nor do we believe that the human body is in any way sinful in its structure.  We believe that our bodies are “fearfully and wonderfully made” and that our God is an amazing Creator. We respect that there are different personal approaches to modesty among Christians in their private spheres of life. Here at Colorado Heritage, we believe that our dress code is conducive to general modesty without inhibiting personal expression.**

**Care for Our Students** **We love our students, and we understand that our dress code is a small part of the way we care for them. Above all, our concern is for their well-being: physical, mental, emotional, and overall - spiritual. We aim to care for our students in these ways, seeking to get to know them, encouraging them, keeping them in prayer.**

_We often have gently-used dress code items for minimal cost/free at our Reformation Baptist Campus._

![](/api/media/files/2c554c678ce378a91e41a02c5870a058f972bfdd907de87c9b9e3ea0c1baf545.webp)

pages.label: Electronics Policy
pages.title: Electronics Policy | Colorado Heritage
pages.description: Review expectations for student electronics at Colorado Heritage.
pages.markdown:
Purpose of the Colorado Heritage Electronics Policy

_Colorado Heritage believes that although modern communication technology offers many benefits_ to the user, this same technology is the gateway to much mental, spiritual, and physical damage with its ever-crowded highway of alluring worldly thoughts, its ungodly philosophies and solutions, temptations, dishonest representations of life, and sometimes, with simply just too much screen time.

_Colorado Heritage remembers the days_ when free time was spent talking with people who were physically present, when books were read, when young people engaged in playing tangible games together such as chess, checkers, etc. Life, relationships, and activities were **not** “experienced” via looking at a 4x6 screen while much of the surrounding environment, and, yes, people actually present, were tuned out. The need to determine who we are and how we measure up to everyone else was not at a desperate and frantic level like it is today. Research abounds that reveals a constant rise in depression linked to cell phone use. Our young people’s peers and counselors are quite often other internet users, famous or not, who fill their minds and hearts with bleak and hopeless messages and beliefs.

_The Colorado Heritage Electronics Policy not only helps to create a distraction free_ classroom environment, but also gives our students a healthy hour or two away from the addiction cell phones and other devices can be, giving our students an opportunity to look up, look around, communicate with those around them, read a tangible book, play those real board games, etc.

_Beyond CHESS walls, we encourage adults and children alike to leave the cell phone, the tablet, and the computer behind in their daily routine_. Use these great inventions only for necessary things, and then only minimally. Look up, look at each other, talk, read books, read out loud together, play board games, play outside, take a walk, paint, draw, write, cook together. Rediscover the real world.

**Colorado Heritage Electronics Policy**

- _Cell Phones/Smart Watches:_ Students are not permitted to use cell phones or have/wear smart watches on campus (or on school-sanctioned field trips and activities). Students will be permitted to use the school phone in case of emergencies. We understand students may have a cell phone in their possession for a variety of reasons. **If a cell phone/smart watch is seen or heard on campus, it will be confiscated by a staff member and will be released only to a parent.**

- _Urgent Communication_ s: If a parent needs to reach the student for an urgent matter, the parent will contact the office or principal who will then relay the message to the student.

- _Laptops/Tablets in the Classroom_: Teachers may give permission for a student to use a laptop/tablet in their classroom for schoolwork.

- _Laptops/Tables in Study Hall_: Students may use laptops/tablets for schoolwork during Study Hall if they receive permission from either the Study Hall Monitor or the principal.  The screen of the laptop or tablet will be visible to the Study Hall Monitor or principal while the student uses the device.

- _Listening Devices/Earbuds/Headsets_ may not be used while on campus unless the student is with the parent in a non-study hall setting.

- _Gaming Devices:_ Devices that are specifically for gaming are not to be used while on campus.

pages.description: Review Colorado homeschool law resources and CHESS support for families.
pages.markdown:
### **Colorado Homeschool Law**

Homeschooling laws differ from state to state. Colorado is one of over 20 states in the United States considered to have low homeschool regulations.

In Colorado, there are three options under which you can legally homeschool.

1. Report to a public school district.

2. Membership in an Independent School such as CHESS.

3. Homeschool with a certified teacher.


For more detailed information on these options, please see [HSLDA](https://hslda.org/legal/colorado).

**Homeschool Services**

# Education is one of the greatest gifts that our Lord has given to us.  In His word He has shown us the importance of teaching our children to fear and serve Him, as admonished in Deuteronomy 6:4-9.

* * *

## high school Diploma Program\*

Colorado Heritage's High School Diploma Program provides a structured guide of basic requirements and achievable goals while allowing parents to individualize the scope and sequence of their student’s education. The goal of the Diploma Program is to support the parents, challenge the students, and substantiate the skills that the student has acquired. Colorado Heritage's Diploma Program provides students with a verification of their work in a private school transcript.

[Join Colorado Heritage's Diploma Program](https://www.coloradoheritage.org/diploma-program) [→](https://www.coloradoheritage.org/diploma-program)

## INDEPENDENT school\*

While enrolled in the Colorado Heritage Education School System's Independent School you will have the benefit of receiving "umbrella school" services(record keeping, communication with school districts) through our dedicated, experienced, and professional staff who know and support the family-focused, discipleship-centered, home-instruction model.  Colorado Heritage's Independent School enrollment gives you the designation of being enrolled in a private school according to the State of Colorado.

[Join Colorado Heritage's Independent School](https://www.coloradoheritage.org/independent-school) [→](https://www.coloradoheritage.org/independent-school)

* * *

## Enrichment Academy (eA)\*

For 25 years, Colorado Heritage has been offering quality enrichment classes for students from kindergarten through twelfth grade in order to meet the academic needs of homeschooling families.

The academy also offers great opportunities for meeting and fellowshipping with like-minded homeschoolers.

[Register for Classes](https://www.coloradoheritage.org/enrichment-academy) [→](https://www.coloradoheritage.org/enrichment-academy)

\* [Here](https://www.coloradoheritage.org/s/CHESS-Overview.pdf) is a visual representation of what Colorado Heritage is and what we offer.

Our Purpose

### Our Purpose

Colorado Heritage Education School System (CHESS) is a private Christian school designed to meet the needs of homeschooling families throughout Colorado, across the United States, and internationally. Since 1991 Colorado Heritage has sought to come alongside and assist, equip, and encourage parents and their children as they seek to follow God’s call in education.

We partner with parents through our Independent School, Diploma Program, and Academy. Our purpose and driving force behind each of these programs is to assist parents in giving their children a Christ-centered education

Our Foundation

### Our Foundation

We believe that God is honored in academic excellence and in life through instruction that is based on a Biblical discipleship model and a Biblical worldview. A personal relationship with the Lord Jesus Christ is necessary to honor God is this way.

We believe the Bible calls parents to be held accountable to and are appointed by God for the determination and overseeing of their children’s education. Our purpose is to come alongside homeschool families with a balanced and cooperatively agreed upon level of assistance.

Colorado Heritage Education School System, _a Private Christian School, who seeks to honor and bring glory to God Almighty, Creator of heaven and earth and to Whom all owe praise and worship for His Holiness, Justice, Goodness, Truth, and Mercy as is clearly communicated in His Word, the 66 books of the Holy Scriptures,_ seeks students from families who are conforming to the biblical pattern for family as found in Holy Scriptures and as specified in the various position statements of this organization. The Colorado Heritage Academy, Diploma Program, and Independent School will consider registrations and applications from families led by a husband and wife (man and woman) or a single parent and/or guardian. To be eligible for acceptance and for continuing enrollment in Colorado Heritage, parents/guardians and students who apply for and who are in our Academy, Independent School and/or Diploma Program must live their life as their birth gender, based on the chromosomes the Lord God Sovereignly gave them before they were in their mother's womb. _"Thine eyes did see my substance, yet being unperfect; and in thy book all my members were written, which in continuance were fashioned, when as yet there was none of them."_ Psalm 139:16

# Meet Our Faculty

### Miss Lilah Barth; B.S. in history from Liberty University. teaches history, drama, and computer graphics

![](/api/media/files/f202eaa187178e68a4a79ea09486b89e073609ea610d4c27be7fea1e7c9f325b.webp)

Miss Barth has blessed CHESS with her amazing teaching skills since December, 2021. She is a born teacher, and her enthusiasm for relaying amazing historical facts and analysis and promoting critical thinking in her students is evident the minute her class starts.

Miss Barth loves to serve her homeschooling students! She, herself, was homeschooled beginning with the 4th grade and up through grade 12. She graduated as a homeschooler, and she loved being homeschooled so much that she says, “Actually, when I hit my final year I didn’t want to graduate, I wanted to continue homeschooling :).” (And if God blesses this Christian young lady with a family, homeschooling is definitely on the agenda!!)

Miss Barth’s credentials include not only her history degree, but also her several past years’, and ongoing work, at a living history museum. She loves the many opportunities there to talk about history and to study it. Miss Barth also spends much time on the side studying history, including a current study of church history.

**Miss Barth on history**: History in general is such a fun subject to teach. There’s so much to explore, and inspiring my students to get excited and curious about the past is probably one of my favorite things to do. I love the look students get when something just clicks with them. History has so many complexities. When I get questions or that moment where I can audibly hear “oh” in the class makes me so excited. One thing I also love about CHESS is that I can teach history from a Christian standpoint, and just be honest about my opinions. For example, I’m preparing to teach Colorado history \[at CHESS\], which means I have to talk about Native Americans. At the museum I can’t share my opinion on this very morally complex issue, but at CHESS I can teach that God owns the land and sovereignly has control over who is living on it. It’s such a blessing.

**Favorite Bible Verse**: There are so many amazing Bible verses I don’t have one…I have many! My favorite quote from church history though is, “You contribute nothing to your salvation except the sin that made it necessary.” This is from Jonathan Edwards, my favorite Puritan preacher.

**Hobbies/Interests**: I have too many :). I am an avid audiobook listener, artist (digital and sketching), a wannabe novel writer, and playwright. I also love dancing (folk, square, and line dances), and over the summer I teach middle school and high school kids’ theater.

* * *

### Mrs. SHANA CHAVEZ; b.s. IN eLEMENTARY eDUCATION & MATHEMATICS FROM BOB JONES UNIVERSITY. CHOIR ASSISTANT/instructor, Elementary Math, SEWING/crafts

![](/api/media/files/a8eac18c5582dd0f3a05815dc2730fc06a50ca91ada6e4c972a9117c2b0d06a7.webp)

Mrs. Chavez has been teaching and volunteering for Colorado Heritage Education School System since 2017. She is a veteran homeschool mom as well as a dedicated pastor’s wife.

Mrs. Chavez’s love for the Lord and her joyful use of the gifts and abilities He has given her is a continual blessing for our students and families.

Mrs. Chavez’s lunchtime snack shop is always a hit with our students!

**Mrs. Chavez on Christian Education and Homeschooling:** I taught in Christian schools for four years before the Lord blessed my husband, David, and I with children.  We always knew that we wanted to homeschool.  We have taught two of our children K-12 and have just one more year with the youngest.  It has been a blessing to have the privilege of seeing our daughters grow and pursue the different areas for which the Lord has equipped each of them.  The older two went on to earn an Associate’s degree and a Master’s degree from Chambers College.  Both are serving the Lord.  Praise be to Him!

I have taught a variety of "fun" classes at CHESS over the years: Sewing, knitting, crocheting, Math Lab, Patch the Pirate Club, and Elementary Choir.  I enjoy tying all subjects to the wonderful works of God and tailoring instruction to the learning style of each student.  I have especially enjoyed tutoring individuals in math and seeing them grasp the challenging concepts.

**Favorite Verse:** Psalm 62:5-8 "My soul, wait thou only upon God; for my expectation is from Him.  He only is my rock and my salvation:  He is my defense; I shall not be moved.  And God is my salvation and glory:  The rock of my strength, and my refuge,  is in God.  Trust in Him at all times; ye people, pour out your heart before Him: God is a refuge for us."

* * *

### Mr. Joshua Franklin, B.A. in History from Colorado State University, Co-Author of _America from the Beginning, A U.S. History Curriculum for Grades 3 - 8_. history teacher

![](/api/media/files/b6520e12390dd6398bbf4a6eb837fb1de02fcbaceaf1a07a0513a2e092f70c21.webp)

**Mr. Franklin’s homeschooling journey**: I was homeschooled from beginning to end. My wife, Rachel, and I homeschool our two children (Admittedly, Rachel does most of the work).

Mr. Franklin loves his history classes and enjoys helping students learn to analyze and critically assess resource content, and then to clearly articulate what they have learned, both in speaking and writing.

Mr. Franklin understands the importance of teaching and learning history from a Biblical point of view, and from a historically correct and frank lens. Mr. Franklin has been teaching for CHESS since 2012.

* * *

### Mrs. Amy Kearns, B.A. in Sociology. Math Teacher\*

![](/api/media/files/2dbc9f5f66504564754d2756e5e4b290615888712882b220e47b2d956a3f739d.webp)

**Mrs. Kearns’ Homeschooling Journey:** “I have been homeschooling my children since before my oldest was in kindergarten. Neither my husband nor I had been homeschooled. In fact, neither of us even knew homeschooling was a thing. Then, as new Christians, we encountered a homeschooling family of nine. I was so impressed with those homeschooled kids. They were very capable of talking to all ages, older and younger than themselves. They were amazingly socialized! That's when we knew that we would homeschool. We have encountered so many joys through the art and discipline of homeschooling our children. We've encountered some heartbreaks as well, but the benefits have always shown themselves to outweigh the doubts that sometimes arise. We've now homeschooled for 16+ years and have four more years to go before our youngest graduates from high school.

“I have a BA in Sociology. That being said, I do not recommend college for all students. I believe that college is a waste of time and money for a large population of kids. I thank God for leading me and guiding me through my life even before I acknowledged His existence. I thank Him and His ability to save me and all those who accept Him into their hearts. I met my husband in college through the Lord's leading. However, that is the only real use to my college career. IF a student KNOWS what he or she wants to do, and it requires college, then, by all means, this student should go to college and get that degree. But no one should go to college just because that's what everyone does, or because the student doesn't know what else to do. However, with the difficult post high school decisions students sometimes face, they can also have the confidence that God can work miracles ‘and we know that all things work together for good to those who love God, to those who are the called according to His purpose.’ Romans 8:28”

**Mrs. Kearns on Math:** I was a good student. I always wanted to please my teachers. I was always a good tester. Sometimes I even tested well by guessing without knowing the material. (That got me into a bind once, so it's not necessarily a good thing.) I never memorized the basic math facts as a child. That made math more difficult the older I got. By the time I got to long division, I felt sunk. In long division, you have dividing, multiplying, _and_ subtraction. If you're completing each and every problem while counting on your fingers, you are setting yourself up for a lot of hard work and wasted time. Then I went into Pre-Algebra. All the sudden, there were letters in math. It was so much fun! (Yes, I do hear myself and understand that this is a sentiment not shared by many.) Math was still lots of hard work for me. I often compared myself to my Valedictorian brother. He was so smart - and everything, learning-wise, seemed to come so naturally to him. I even had a Chemistry teacher say to me in class in front of my classmates, "You really aren't as smart as your brother, are you?" I thought that needing to work hard to understand my schoolwork made me a lesser student. But, in fact, it helped me learn how to learn, and it set me up for success in life. (My brother failed out of college in his first attempt because he didn't learn how to learn in high school.) Math was work for me, sometimes hard work. But I enjoyed it and the sense of accomplishment it gave me. I feel that this hard work has helped me be a better math teacher than I would have been if math had come easily to me. I can show my students how to understand and work the new concepts because I also struggled with these same concepts at some point.

**Final thoughts from Mrs. Kearns:** I am so very thankful that God has worked in my life, led me, and saved me. It's wonderful to know that He is in control, and that I don't have to be. I can leave the anxiety behind and "be anxious for nothing, but in everything by prayer and supplication, with thanksgiving, \[I can let my\] requests be made known to God, and let the peace of God, which surpasses all understanding \[guard my heart and mind\] through Jesus Christ." Philippians 4:6-7 "God is \[my\] refuge and strength, a very present help in trouble. Therefore \[I\] will not fear, even though the earth be removed, and though the mountains be carried into the midst of the sea; though it's waters roar and be troubled, though the mountains shake with its swelling." Psalm 46:1-3

_\*Mrs. Kearns is also our talented and proficient Admissions Coordinator for the Independent School and Academy, coordinates our Standardized Testing Service and also serves as our Diploma Program Registrar. Mrs. Kearns has served at CHESS since 2019._

* * *

### **Mr. Andrew Kearns, Physical Education**

![](/api/media/files/bc50d13a2e1784e70a698d505dd88e12155005c45c0128dfa8a012a89f14ea63.webp)

**My thoughts on Home Education and Christian Education:** Homeschooling is a blessing. I consider myself very blessed to have been raised as a homeschooled child. As a homeschooled student, I learned how to do things in ways that others wouldn’t at first consider. Homeschooling helps students to think outside the box as well as to comfortably talk to others outside of our age group. There are many more blessings that come with homeschooling, and it is, by far, my favorite way to be taught. (And if God blesses me with a family, you can bet that my children will be homeschooled.)

Christian education is even better, because aside from the benefits I gained from homeschooling, I was also raised and taught to love God and all of His blessings. One of the several things I learned from this Christian education that has helped me through my personal season of singleness is that God has a plan for me and that all I need to do is submit to Him and His plan. Romans 8:28 is one of several verses that helps me to remember this. “And we know that God causes everything to work together for the good of those who love God and are called according to his purpose for them.” (NLT)

I attended the CHESS Academy for many of my classes throughout my homeschool journey and graduated with honors from the CHESS High School Diploma Program. CHESS was significantly helpful in my Christian journey. Every time I think of the benefits of CHESS (i.e., Christian education, homeschool support, etc.) one stands out to me above all the rest: the fellowship with other students. I wouldn’t have met any of my dearest friends if it wasn’t for CHESS.

**My personal favorite verse(s):** One of my favorite set of verses of all time is Romans 8:17-18, “And since we are his children, we are his heirs. In fact, together with Christ we are heirs of God’s glory. But if we are to share his glory, we must also share his suffering. Yet what we suffer now is nothing compared to the glory he will reveal to us later.” (NLT) These verses are tied with so many other favorite verses. So, essentially, I’m saying that I don’t have a favorite verse or set of verses. I do, however, have a favorite chapter of the Bible. Romans 8 is by far my favorite chapter of the Bible of all time. In nearly every single one of my school papers, I found some way to sneak at least one verse from Romans 8 into it.

**My Hobbies:** I have many hobbies. A few of my favorites are listening to music, gaming, art, writing, and brainstorming for writing ideas.

**My Goals as a Teacher:** My goals for the P.E classes are to teach the students to grow, not only in their body, but also in their mind, and especially their spirit. I want to teach my students to think in ways that honor the Lord and to grow themselves in such a way that they are more capable of honoring the Lord throughout their daily life.

**Current Academic Pursuits:** Attending AIMS Community College for an Associates in Computer Science, towards a Bachelor’s in Computer Science in an out-of-state college.

* * *

### mr. Paul leDuc, b.A. in pastoral ministry from Chambers College. teaches bible classes for grades k-2 and 3-5, and Junior High Literature; coordinates our school chapels

![](/api/media/files/e190dff6e17571a655cc9ccf80bfede2dba0966e89f9f15524fa94d6bafda9ea.webp)

In 2015, my parents enrolled me in Colorado Heritage where I learned the value of a solid education that is Christ-centered. I graduated from the Colorado Heritage Diploma Program in 2021 and graduated from Chambers College in 2026 with a Bachelor of Arts degree in Pastoral Ministry. I am trusting in the Lord to guide me in future plans.

**Mr. leDuc’s Favorite Bible passage:** I love Philippians 2:5-11 as I believe it summarizes the Gospel message and the calling of the Christian in Christ. _“Let this mind be in you which was also in Christ Jesus, who, being in the form of God, did not consider it robbery to be equal with God, but made Himself of no reputation, taking the form of a bondservant, and coming in the likeness of men. And being found in appearance as a man, He humbled Himself and became obedient to the point of death, even the death of the cross. Therefore, God also has highly exalted Him and given Him the name which is above every name, that at the name of Jesus every knee should bow, of those in heaven, and of those on earth, and of those under the earth, and that every tongue should confess that Jesus Christ is Lord, to the glory of God the Father.”_

**Mr. leDuc’s interests:** I love anything Bible-related and enjoy having long in-depth conversations with people about the Scriptures. Outside of that, I enjoy hanging out with my friends and doing a bit of everything with them, whether it be hiking, turtle-hunting, board games, sketching pictures of each other, trying weird foods, going on scary rides at amusement parks, and many other such adventures. I am always up to trying something new at least once.

* * *

### Mrs. Annie Nelson, B.A. in Education from Northland Baptist Bible College. Teaches Literature classes and kitchen home economics; advisory board member

![](/api/media/files/bfec48127c139ea5442b999e1fef3dc7bd0b0a256b104774ebcdb73c760d9069.webp)

I was given a solid Christian education by parents who believed in the value of a Christ-centered education. I loved books from an early age and read my way through several books each week. My life, you could say, was shaped by stories. After graduating from Northland Baptist Bible College with a BA in education, I married a rancher from Northern Colorado, and God graciously gave us ten children, all of whom needed educating! I have been a homeschool mom for thirty years now, and they have been sanctifying years where God has met me in my deepest failures and days of need. We also discovered CHESS, where other faithful Christians mentored and taught my kids—huge blessing!

I began teaching a literature class in my home in 2003 for my children and their friends, and when I was invited by CHESS to teach with them in 2007, I quickly discovered how much better it is to not have to clean your house each time before class. 😊My love for good stories has only deepened, and I have a passion to see my students shaped as they read and question and write about the beauty found in literary classics.

I also love dirt (because flowers) and working with my hands to make delicious food or organize books in a bookcase in a way that piques one’s interest. My thirteen grandchildren (soon to be sixteen) take up a bountiful portion of my time and affection, and I try to be available for my five married children, and my five unmarried children. Life is full and overflowing with the goodness of God and there is truly never a dull moment.

Mrs. Nelson has been teaching and volunteering for CHESS since 2008.

* * *

### Mr. Noah Nelson, A.A. in Liberal Arts and B.S. in Interdisciplinary Studies with concentrations in Global Leadership and Media Production. teaches financial stewardship, civic classes, speech and debate, and computer applications

![](/api/media/files/f3e92bc12bed5335deea4a5d06eda13780695ff759fb14cbb74174617a7ba272.webp)

Homeschooling played a vital role in shaping Mr. Nelson’s character and love for learning. From an early age, his mother cultivated in him and his siblings a deep appreciation for literature by reading to them daily, while his great-aunt’s phonics curriculum laid the foundation for a lifelong love of reading. Growing up on the family farm further enriched this education, instilling responsibility, diligence, and the value of hard work. Noah also gained practical experience in stewardship and discipline by managing a small roadside stand that sold the farm’s fruits and vegetables.

A hallmark of Noah’s homeschooling experience was the consistent integration of Scripture into every subject. He was taught to view all of life through the lens of God’s ownership of all things—that every field of study, including mathematics, is grounded in the reality of God’s existence and character. Without God, mathematics and reason would not exist, for they reflect the order and logic of a sovereign and rational Creator. Mr. Nelson is a graduate of Colorado Heritage Education School System and was blessed that the philosophy of Christian education he received at CHESS mirrored and came alongside the Christian education he received at home.

For Mr. Nelson, homeschooling is significant not only for its academic benefits but also for its theological foundation: it preserves the God-given responsibility of parents to make sure that they themselves (or those they authorize) train their children in the nurture and admonition of the Lord.

Among his favorite portions of Scripture are the Psalms, with Psalm 103 being one of his favorites. Outside of his studies and work, Noah enjoys photography, classical music, and reading.

Mr. Nelson is currently prayerfully considering pursuing a master’s degree in Christian education.

* * *

### PASTOR BAXTER ONG, B.A. in CHRISTIAN MINISTRY from chambers college; Master of divinity from shepherds theological seminary. teaches: bible, church history, apologetics, logic, philosophy, hermeneutics, greek and hebrew. board member

![](/api/media/files/f7ab69a44189f93b477ad5cb3ae76dd5b77fa87bfeb2f1d94a5a871ddfe2820f.webp)

Baxter was born a few years after CHESS was founded by his parents, Pastor Steve and Teri Ong. He grew up attending classes at CHESS and graduated from the Honors Diploma Program. He was co-enrolled in Chambers College his junior and senior years and graduated at age 19 with his Bachelor of Arts of Christian Ministry degree. While in Chambers College, he sat under the teaching of Dr. Doug Bookman, a faculty member at Shepherds Theological Seminary in Cary, North Carolina.

Baxter earned his Master of Divinity degree from Shepherds and returned to Greeley.  He served as associate pastor with his father at Reformation Baptist Church for a year, then becoming the senior pastor in 2023.

He loves teaching Bible, apologetics, logic and philosophy classes. He is most passionate about teaching hermeneutics, so students are able to rightly understand and apply Scripture for themselves and have a defense against unsound interpretations.

**Hobbies:** Baxter loves doing artwork in various mediums, playing games, and watching good biopics.

Pastor Baxter Ong has been teaching for CHESS since 2018. He is the pastor of Reformation Baptist Church as well as the president of Chambers College.

* * *

### Mrs. Teri Ong, B.A. in Church Music Education from Denver Baptist Bible College, M.A. in Elementary Education from University of Northern Colorado, M.A. in Christian Liberal Arts from Chambers College. music teacher; board member

![](/api/media/files/95af9efa77a8c2b40b6633b2d4c86e5cfcd117809163b0687b2a3ed4e529a184.webp)

My husband, Steve, and I founded CHESS in 1991. I have been teaching a variety of classes at CHESS ever since, but my forte is music. I teach the choir and ensemble classes and oversee a fall semester and a spring semester concert each year.

We homeschooled all seven of our children from beginning to end.  Two of them you are likely to run into in CHESS, Baxter Ong, who is the pastor of Reformation Baptist Church, and Alice Wishart, who teaches a variety of classes.

Like Mrs. Charles Spurgeon, I was a pastor's wife for 46 years (until my husband went to heaven) and now I am a pastor's mother! One of my guiding scriptures is Ephesians 2:8-10. I hope to continue to walk in the works God has foreordained for me at CHESS.

**Hobbies and Interests:** My hobbies are all things creative-- writing of all sorts, sewing, painting, and of course, music. I play violin in the Loveland Orchestra, one of my chief delights.

* * *

### Mrs. polly salzmann, weight training

![](/api/media/files/59f646aff3df8ccfc22b1a788e47de1923d5e3aef6d7bd7e0f2795e6ebb7fafc.webp)

I am one of seven children. My father was a recovering alcoholic who came to the Lord later in life, and as a result, I saw firsthand how God's mercy and grace can change the dynamic of a family for generations. I also learned how to be hospitable, even when you had little to nothing to share, and the impact that had on the people my father served.

My amazing husband, Dennis, has made it possible for me to homeschool our children. My daughter is a nurse, my middle son is a licensed EMT/Firefighter, and I am homeschooling our youngest to complete his high school years in three years instead of four. I have a heart for teenagers and the specific challenges that they face. I am also hopeful for them and the future because they were 'born for such a time as this.'

My favorite Bible verse changes all the time because the Lord is always doing a new work in me and drawing me to certain things at certain times. However, today, I'm drawn to James 1:17. "Every good and perfect gift is from above, from the Father of lights, in whom there is no change or shifting shadow." How encouraging! In this world of changing politics, social norms, pandemics, and wars, our

God does not change, and every good and beautiful thing that we have and encounter comes from Him. He gives us good things, not because we need them or deserve them but from the abundance of His love for us. What a gift to be servants of the King!

* * *

### Mr. Cliff Smart, b.a. bIOLOGY, minors in chemistry and psychology. science teacher

![](/api/media/files/388b35b319652bba5c5393baa3d8e31a4f153e2bfe497a8d30685f4a80d93e68.webp)

Mr. Smart has been a science freak all his life, and it’s only gotten worse!  For over 40 years he worked as an analyst in testing laboratories and as a chemist and environmentalist in a power plant.

He and his wife, Christina, homeschooled their three children from kindergarten to college, and both Mr. and Mrs. Smart have taught in co-ops, enrichment programs, and now both are teaching at Colorado Heritage! (See Chris Smart’s bio).

**Mr. Smart’s Interests:** Mr. Smart enjoys a wide range of interests, including astronomy, ISS flybys & space flight, studying God’s Creation, firearms, Ham radio, fixin’ things, history, current events, politics, reading, and pursuing the Lord.

**Favorite Bible Verse:** Eph 6:10 & 11, “Be strong in the Lord and His mighty power. Put on the full armor of God so that you can take your stand against the devil’s schemes.”

**Mr. Smart on Christian Repurposing:** “I asked God to ‘re-purpose’ me after retirement, and now, I am teaching science to young people!  I am blessed to have been given this opportunity and am THRILLED to be working with junior and high school students!”

Mr. Smart has been teaching for CHESS since 2023 but also lent a helping hand to CHESS in former years as an advisory board member.

* * *

### Mrs. Chris Smart, B.A. in christian ministry from Chambers College. Writing teacher, grade levels 3-5, 6-8, 9-12; history teacher for grades k-2, 3-5

![](/api/media/files/1412af488ca59b539842e7621c03c9d8d588341dca25dade8532d8a0f61a71cf.webp)

Mrs. Smart is a veteran homeschooler who has taught private and enrichment classes for over 26 years, including 14 years with CHESS!

She and her husband, Cliff, homeschooled their three children.  All of the kids graduated from college and are now busy being adults.

Though the Smarts are done raising their children, life has not slowed down!  Mrs. Smart continually finds herself engaged in family, ministry, and her forever puppy, Marty; plus, she enjoys a great many interests including gardening, cooking, and crafts.

Following God’s direction, she continues serving the homeschool community through teaching at CHESS.

Although Mrs. Smart loves to teach many subjects, her favorite is writing.  Mrs. Smart truly loves helping students discover that writing does not need to be a chore; **it can actually be fun!**

Mrs. Smart has been teaching for CHESS since 2009. She also blessed us with her care and wisdom for several years as a board member.

* * *

### Mrs. Stacey Solanyk; B.A. in Art & Design from Grand Valley State University.  Zoology TEACHER

![](/api/media/files/3d51c2dcf8c33cb4c57eecd562b0d94ea21d6a621d77b9dbe199746aff06c5b9.webp)

I was raised in a Christian home on a dairy farm in west Michigan and moved to Colorado to teach.  I taught a multigrade classroom of grades 1-3 and junior high art classes for five years in a local Christian school.  I married my husband, Eric, and God has blessed us with six children.  Our children attended Christian school until we began homeschooling a few years ago.  After one year of homeschooling, we started using Colorado Heritage, which has been a huge help in the education of our children.  We are thankful for the godly, dedicated teachers at CHESS and for the opportunity for our children to learn with Christian friends.  We appreciate the balance of educating at home and at school that Colorado Heritage provides.  This will be my first year teaching for Colorado Heritage, and I am looking forward to serving here where our family has been blessed.

**Hobbies and Interests:** Eric and I and our children live on an acreage in Northern Colorado.  We love being outside taking care of our animals and property and spending time together.  I also enjoy playing the piano, running, gardening, oil painting, photography, reading, and teaching.

**On Christian Education:** Christian education is important because the teacher’s worldview influences what information is taught and how it is presented.  Our goal as Christian parents and educators is to raise Christ-centered, spiritually mature children who find their identity in Christ, who are able to think biblically, comparing all thoughts and ideas to scripture, and who are well-prepared to lead thankful lives of service and purpose.

I am very thankful for my Savior Jesus Christ and for the Lord’s provision and care for me and my family.  We trust Him and endeavor to glorify Him in all that we do, say, and think _._  The Psalms, the Book of Isaiah, and gospel-centered sermons and music have been a source of great encouragement for me through the many seasons of life.

_“Wherefore seeing we also are compassed about with so great a cloud of witnesses, let us lay aside every weight, and the sin which doth so easily beset us, and let us run with patience the race that is set before us, looking unto Jesus the author and finisher of our faith; who for the joy that was set before him endured the cross, despising the shame, and is set down at the right hand of the throne of God.”  (Hebrews 12:1-2_)

* * *

### Mrs. Alice Wishart, B.A. Chambers College; majored in Communication and minored in Education. art teacher

![](/api/media/files/1576cf3bac6c08f2d9320e0e4eb05c6f9c402cbdfaf20698f5b38acd93bb4693.webp)

Mrs. Wishart was not only homeschooled, but she was also born the year that CHESS was founded by her parents, Pastor and Mrs. Ong!! She was happily homeschooled by her parents from kindergarten through high school, and she took CHESS classes from age 4 - 18. Alice graduated from the CHESS Diploma Program as a Highest Honors, All Star Student.

**Mrs. Wishart on homeschooling and on creativity:** “I am in the process of homeschooling my very own children and plan to continue for the foreseeable future. I loved being homeschooled, and I am enjoying the journey myself of homeschooling.

“I have always loved being creative. I enjoy beautiful things. And I love understanding why they are beautiful - from book art to fine art. God has created us to be makers, and it is delightful to use that in re-creating His lovely world in the form of art. In recent years, I have taken several mini, online art classes to keep advancing my own skills.”

**My favorite Bible verse:** Psalm 73:28: But as for me, the nearness of God is good for me; I have made the Lord God my refuge, So that I may tell of all Your works.

**My hobbies and interests:** Making things. I love painting, drawing, floral arranging, house renovation projects, building with wood, exploring nature with my husband and kids. I enjoy playing my instruments cello, piano, violin, and plan to learn the hammer dulcimer. I love good Bible studies and playing a variety of board games.

Mrs. Wishart has been teaching for CHESS since 2017.

* * *

Stay tuned for more bios on the rest of our wonderful teachers!!

pages.markdown:
![mountains-2535733_1920.jpg](/api/media/files/db4db2de4702c48d17b92909478477d4fdf1fc51654b4adfcffc4a60e168a44b.webp)

Our History

Colorado Heritage Education School System was originally founded as a ministry of Victory Baptist Church (now called Reformation Baptist Church) in Greeley, Colorado, by Pastor Stephen and Mrs. Teri Ong in 1991. The Ongs, pioneers of home education, began home educating their children in 1986. Stephen and Teri Ong were influential in helping to broaden home education freedoms in Colorado before home education was recognized as a viable means of education in Colorado. Colorado Heritage in its early years offered art and choir classes once a week to homeschooling families as well as record keeping and general supervision through its Independent School.

Today, Colorado Heritage operates as a 501C private Christian school serving families not only through our Independent School but also through our quality Academy and High School Diploma Program. Over the years, we have had the joy of seeing our Academy students learn and grow in the knowledge of the Lord through our Bible classes and as they pursue proficiency in our Science, English, Math, History, Art, and many of our other classes. Our High School Diploma Program has graduated over five hundred high school seniors with an average of 75% of graduates going on to college, with many others pursuing the trades.

Colorado Heritage is blessed with dedicated Christian faculty, staff, volunteers, and board members. The families that join us in our halls find great fellowship one with another, encouraging each other in the worthy calling of Christian-based homeschooling.

### **As Colorado Heritage continues to grow, seeking to bless and strengthen homeschooling families and the community, we look to the mercy and grace of our LORD and King.**

pages.markdown:
### Testimonials

> “When my daughter decided she wanted to homeschool her high school years, we were looking for a school to umbrella us during our journey.  After we interviewed with CHESS, we decided to go further and enroll my daughter in the CHESS Diploma Program for the accountability and an actual private school diploma at graduation. She thrived in the CHESS environment.  I watched as her joy returned.  The Godly aspect in each class grew my daughter spiritually, which is priceless.  I cannot say enough good about the teachers and Mrs. Brown, the principal, because their care for my daughter went above and beyond what she would have received in a secular school setting.  The classes offered at CHESS were a perfect complement to our home classes.  I am absolutely certain this school was a Godsend for which we will always be grateful and thankful.”

— Kortney, Greeley CO

> “I recommend CHESS for several reasons. My children and I appreciate the relationships that they’ve made there. I have a daughter in nursing school, and she counts several of the friendships that she made at CHESS as best friends in adulthood. My sons, a senior and an 8th grader, also greatly value the friends that they’ve made there. As a parent, I love knowing the families of their friends, because you can walk through raising kids together, and the mom fellowship is awesome! CHESS has a great curriculum and Diploma Program. The staff is incredibly patient and gracious while they guide one through the processes required for the Independent School and Diploma Program. Having a diploma, from a school, made my daughter’s entrance into nursing school seamless. CHESS is very supportive of parents, and we can choose which classes to take with CHESS and which classes we would like to teach our kids at home. We especially love Mr. Ong’s Bible classes and Mrs. Smart’s writing classes. We live 45 minutes from CHESS and have been attending since 2018. We count the drive as an easy sacrifice for so many wonderful benefits! ”

— Polly, Firestone CO

> “CHESS is truly a blessing to our family. As a new family to homeschooling, we were helped by CHESS to navigate the process of what is required to help keep us on track for our high school student. We utilize the Independent School, High School Diploma Program, Academy, and Standardized Testing. The Christ-centered teaching and staff are such an encouragement for us. My daughter’s favorite thing besides the wonderful friends she has made, is that her English teacher prays every day before class. Switching to CHESS was the best decision we made for our high school student!”

— Crystal, Johnstown CO

> “​​​​​​​I don’t know where to begin to thank you for all you’ve done. I am pretty sure we would not have been able to home school all the way through high school without CHESS’s diploma program. Your direction, encouragement, and influence on our son caused him to reach higher and accomplish more academically and spiritually than he would have ever been able to do without you.”

— Michelle, Bailey CO

> “We are thankful for all you are doing to help us teach our kids in the nurture and admonition of the Lord. ”

— David, Cheyenne WY

> “We are so thankful for the Christian emphasis at Colorado Heritage and for the caliber of the teachers. We graduated our four students from your Diploma Program, and we can truly say that the experience from start to finish was a blessing! I highly recommend this school to homeschooling parents or to those who are thinking about homeschooling and who want their high school student(s) to receive a quality education which is firmly housed in traditional Biblical values and beliefs. ”

— Mary, Nunn CO

> “Your guidance and prayers have been a tremendous blessing!”

— Gordon & Robin, Brighton CO

> “We appreciate your willingness to work with us and offer the flexibility you have.”

— Sandy, Greeley CO

Here are three ways

you can financially support Colorado Heritage, Christian Education, and our students!

* * *

1. ### You can DONATE to our SCHOLARSHIP fund


- $270.00 will pay for one elementary class for one student for an entire school year.

- $430.00 will pay for one two-day junior high class for one junior high student for an entire school year.

- $335.00 will pay for one one-day class for one high school student for an entire school year.

- $480.00 will pay for one two-day class for one high school student an entire school year.

- $75.00 will pay for one tech fee for one student for the entire year.
